3	#   1. neurosymbolic-rl: Neurosymbolic reasoning + RL/GRPO
4	#   2. reward-shaping: Reward shaping for code/formal verification
5	#   3. mutation-testing: Mutation testing in software engineering
6	#   4. intensional-analysis: Intensional program analysis
7	#   5. reward-hacking: Reward hacking / overoptimization
8	#   6. fol-formalization: FOL/Prolog formalization with LLMs

10	papers:
11	
12	  # ============================================================
13	  # Category 1: Neurosymbolic reasoning + RL/GRPO
14	  # ============================================================
15	
16	  - id: deepseek-r1
17	    title: "DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning"
18	    authors: "DeepSeek-AI"
19	    year: 2025
20	    venue: "arXiv 2501.12948 / Nature 2025"
21	    category: neurosymbolic-rl
22	    role: method-component
23	    relevance: >
24	      Demonstrates that pure RL (GRPO) can incentivize reasoning in LLMs without SFT.
25	      STA builds on the same GRPO framework but replaces binary outcome reward with
26	      intensional structural reward for neurosymbolic formalization.
27	    key_finding: >
28	      DeepSeek-R1-Zero trained via GRPO alone achieves 71% on AIME 2024,
29	      showing emergent chain-of-thought reasoning from RL alone.
30	
31	  - id: deepseekmath
32	    title: "DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models"
33	    authors: "Zhihong Shao, Peiyi Wang, Qihao Zhu, Runxin Xu, et al."
34	    year: 2024
35	    venue: "arXiv 2402.03300"
36	    category: neurosymbolic-rl
37	    role: method-component
38	    relevance: >
39	      Introduces GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization), the RL algorithm
40	      used in STA training. GRPO eliminates the critic model by estimating
41	      baselines from group scores.
42	    key_finding: >
43	      GRPO matches PPO performance while significantly reducing training
44	      resources; improves GSM8K 82.9->88.2% and MATH 46.8->51.7%.
45	
46	  - id: logic-rl
47	    title: "Logic-RL: Unleashing LLM Reasoning with Rule-Based Reinforcement Learning"
48	    authors: "Xian et al."
49	    year: 2025
50	    venue: "arXiv 2502.14768"
51	    category: neurosymbolic-rl
52	    role: direct-competitor
53	    relevance: >
54	      Uses rule-based RL (REINFORCE++) for LLM logical reasoning on synthetic
55	      logic puzzles. Closest competitor to STA's approach of RL for logical
56	      formalization, though Logic-RL uses extensional (answer-correctness)
57	      rewards rather than STA's intensional structural rewards.
58	    key_finding: >
59	      REINFORCE++ outperforms GRPO on logic puzzles with superior stability;
60	      rule-based reward design is critical for RL-based logical reasoning.
61	
62	  - id: mellgren-prolog-grpo
63	    title: "Training Language Models to Use Prolog as a Tool"
64	    authors: "Niklas Mellgren"
65	    year: 2024
66	    venue: "arXiv 2512.07407"
67	    category: neurosymbolic-rl
68	    role: direct-competitor
69	    relevance: >
70	      Uses GRPO to train a 3B LLM to generate Prolog code for reasoning,
71	      directly comparable to STA's approach of GRPO-training a formalizer.
72	      Key difference: uses pass/fail reward vs STA's structural ISR.
73	    key_finding: >
74	      GRPO is effective for teaching small LLMs to use Prolog as a tool
75	      for logical and mathematical reasoning.
76	
77	  - id: satlm
78	    title: "SatLM: Satisfiability-Aided Language Models Using Declarative Prompting"
79	    authors: "Xi Ye et al."
80	    year: 2023
81	    venue: "NeurIPS 2023"
82	    category: neurosymbolic-rl
83	    role: background
84	    relevance: >
85	      Neurosymbolic approach where LLM generates declarative specifications
86	      verified by SAT solver. Similar pipeline to STA (LLM->formal spec->solver)
87	      but uses prompting, not RL training.
88	    key_finding: >
89	      Declarative formulation outperforms imperative program-aided LMs by 23%
90	      on GSM; achieves SoTA on LSAT and BoardgameQA.
91	
92	  # ============================================================
93	  # Category 2: Reward shaping for code/formal verification
94	  # ============================================================
95	
96	  - id: lightman-verify-step
97	    title: "Let's Verify Step by Step"
98	    authors: "Hunter Lightman, Vineet Kosaraju, Yura Burda, et al."
99	    year: 2023
100	    venue: "arXiv 2305.20050 / ICLR 2024"
101	    category: reward-shaping
102	    role: method-component
103	    relevance: >
104	      Establishes that process supervision (step-level reward) outperforms
105	      outcome supervision (final-answer reward) for reasoning. STA's ISR
106	      is analogous: it provides structural process-level signal about which
107	      components of a formalization matter, rather than just pass/fail.
108	    key_finding: >
109	      Process-supervised reward model achieves 78% on MATH, significantly
110	      outperforming outcome-supervised models. Released PRM800K dataset.
111	
112	  - id: reward-shaping-rlhf
113	    title: "Reward Shaping to Mitigate Reward Hacking in RLHF"
114	    authors: "Jiayi Fu, Xuandong Zhao, Chengyuan Yao, et al."
115	    year: 2025
116	    venue: "arXiv 2502.18770"
117	    category: reward-shaping
118	    role: background
119	    relevance: >
120	      Studies reward shaping design principles for RLHF: bounded rewards and
121	      rapid-then-convergent growth. STA's ISR follows these principles
122	      naturally since structural necessity scores are bounded [0,1].
123	    key_finding: >
124	      Two key reward shaping principles: (1) bounded RL reward, (2) rapid
125	      initial growth with gradual convergence. PAR method achieves 5%+
126	      win rate improvement on AlpacaEval 2.0.
127	
128	  - id: rlvr-reasoning
129	    title: "Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs"
130	    authors: "Various"
131	    year: 2025
132	    venue: "arXiv 2506.14245"
133	    category: reward-shaping
134	    role: background
135	    relevance: >
136	      Shows that binary verifiable rewards (pass/fail) can implicitly incentivize
137	      reasoning. STA argues that for neurosymbolic formalization, binary reward
138	      is insufficient and structural reward is needed to avoid reward hacking.
139	    key_finding: >
140	      RLVR with binary verification implicitly teaches correct reasoning
141	      strategies, not just answer matching.
142	
143	  - id: rubric-grpo
144	    title: "Rubric-Grounded Reinforcement Learning: Structured Judge Rewards for Generalizable Reasoning"
145	    authors: "Various"
146	    year: 2025
147	    venue: "arXiv 2605.08061"
148	    category: reward-shaping
149	    role: direct-competitor
150	    relevance: >
151	      Uses structured rubric-based rewards with GRPO, similar in spirit to
152	      STA's structured ISR. Key difference: rubric rewards come from LLM
153	      judges, while ISR comes from solver-based mutation testing.
154	    key_finding: >
155	      Structured multi-dimensional reward signals improve GRPO training
156	      generalization compared to scalar rewards.
157	
158	  # ============================================================
159	  # Category 3: Mutation testing in software engineering
160	  # ============================================================
161	
162	  - id: demillo1978
163	    title: "Hints on Test Data Selection: Help for the Practicing Programmer"
164	    authors: "Richard A. DeMillo, Richard J. Lipton, Frederick G. Sayward"
165	    year: 1978
166	    venue: "Computer 11(4):34-43"
167	    category: mutation-testing
168	    role: background
169	    relevance: >
170	      Foundational paper introducing mutation testing. STA's component
171	      necessity testing directly extends this idea: instead of mutating
172	      source code to test test suites, STA mutates logical formulas
173	      to test component necessity for solver success.
174	    key_finding: >
175	      Introduced mutation testing and the coupling effect hypothesis:
176	      tests that detect simple faults also detect complex faults.
177	
178	  - id: offutt-coupling
179	    title: "Investigations of the Software Testing Coupling Effect"
180	    authors: "A. Jefferson Offutt"
181	    year: 1992
182	    venue: "ACM TOSEM 1(1):5-20"
183	    category: mutation-testing
184	    role: background
185	    relevance: >
186	      Empirically validates the coupling effect hypothesis that underpins
187	      mutation testing. STA's single-component ablation is analogous to
188	      first-order mutation; the coupling effect suggests this suffices.
189	    key_finding: >
190	      Test data killing all first-order mutants killed >99% of second-
191	      and third-order mutants, validating the coupling effect.
192	
193	  - id: jia-harman-survey
194	    title: "An Analysis and Survey of the Development of Mutation Testing"
195	    authors: "Yue Jia, Mark Harman"
196	    year: 2011
197	    venue: "IEEE TSE 37(5):649-678"
198	    category: mutation-testing
199	    role: background
200	    relevance: >
201	      Comprehensive survey of mutation testing covering three decades of
202	      development. Provides theoretical and practical foundation for STA's
203	      adaptation of mutation testing to logical formulas.
204	    key_finding: >
205	      Systematic classification of mutation operators, cost reduction
206	      techniques, and equivalence problem -- all relevant to STA's design
207	      of clause-level ablation operators.
208	
209	  - id: just-mutants-real-faults
210	    title: "Are Mutants a Valid Substitute for Real Faults in Software Testing?"
211	    authors: "Rene Just, Darioush Jalali, Laura Inozemtseva, et al."
212	    year: 2014
213	    venue: "FSE 2014"
214	    category: mutation-testing
215	    role: background
216	    relevance: >
217	      Validates that mutation testing (structural/intensional analysis of
218	      program adequacy) correlates with real fault detection. Supports STA's
219	      premise that structural analysis of formalization components provides
220	      meaningful signal about formalization quality.
221	    key_finding: >
222	      Mutant detection is statistically correlated with real fault detection,
223	      and mutation score is a better predictor of test effectiveness than
224	      code coverage.
225	
226	  - id: llmorpheus
227	    title: "LLMorpheus: Mutation Testing Using Large Language Models"
228	    authors: "Frank Tip, Jon Bell, et al."
229	    year: 2025
230	    venue: "IEEE TSE 2025"
231	    category: mutation-testing
232	    role: background
233	    relevance: >
234	      Uses LLMs to generate realistic code mutants beyond traditional
235	      mutation operators. Shows mutation testing evolving toward
236	      ML-integrated approaches, validating STA's cross-pollination
237	      of mutation testing ideas into ML training.
238	    key_finding: >
239	      LLM-generated mutants simulate real bugs that rule-based operators
240	      cannot produce, improving mutation testing realism.
241	
242	  - id: mutation-guided-meta
243	    title: "Mutation-Guided LLM-based Test Generation at Meta"
244	    authors: "Christopher Foster et al."
245	    year: 2025
246	    venue: "FSE 2025"
247	    category: mutation-testing
248	    role: background
249	    relevance: >
250	      Industrial application of mutation-guided LLM test generation at
251	      Meta. Demonstrates that mutation analysis can guide LLM behavior
252	      in production -- analogous to how STA uses mutation (ablation) to
253	      guide GRPO reward signal.
254	    key_finding: >
255	      Mutation-guided approach generates tests that kill significantly
256	      more mutants than unguided LLM test generation at Meta scale.
257	
258	  - id: mutation-consistency-llm
259	    title: "Mutation-based Consistency Testing for Evaluating the Code Understanding Capability of LLMs"
260	    authors: "Various"
261	    year: 2024
262	    venue: "arXiv 2401.05940"
263	    category: mutation-testing
264	    role: background
265	    relevance: >
266	      Uses code mutations to evaluate LLM code understanding consistency.
267	      Conceptually related to STA: both use systematic code/formula
268	      mutations to assess model capabilities.
269	    key_finding: >
270	      LLMs show significant inconsistency when evaluated on mutated code
271	      variants, suggesting superficial pattern matching.
272	
273	  # ============================================================
274	  # Category 4: Intensional program analysis
275	  # ============================================================
276	
277	  - id: deepmutation
278	    title: "A Probabilistic Framework for Mutation Testing in Deep Neural Networks"
279	    authors: "Various"
280	    year: 2023
281	    venue: "Information and Software Technology 2023"
282	    category: intensional-analysis
283	    role: background
284	    relevance: >
285	      Extends mutation testing to DNN testing with probabilistic mutation
286	      operators. Parallel to STA's extension of mutation testing from
287	      traditional programs to logical formulas.
288	    key_finding: >
289	      Probabilistic mutation framework enables meaningful test adequacy
290	      assessment for neural networks through structural perturbation.
291

293	  # Category 5: Reward hacking / overoptimization
294	  # ============================================================
295	
296	  - id: inform-reward-hacking
297	    title: "InfoRM: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling"
298	    authors: "Various"
299	    year: 2024
300	    venue: "NeurIPS 2024"
301	    category: reward-hacking
302	    role: background
303	    relevance: >
304	      Proposes information-bottleneck approach to detect and mitigate reward
305	      hacking. STA's ISR addresses the same problem differently: by grounding
306	      reward in verifiable structural properties (component necessity), it
307	      reduces the attack surface for reward hacking.
308	    key_finding: >
309	      Variational information bottleneck filters irrelevant features from
310	      reward model; Cluster Separation Index detects reward overoptimization.
311	
312	  - id: mo-grpo
313	    title: "MO-GRPO: Mitigating Reward Hacking of Group Relative Policy Optimization on Multi-Objective Problems"
314	    authors: "CyberAgent AI Lab"
315	    year: 2025
316	    venue: "arXiv 2509.22047"
317	    category: reward-hacking
318	    role: background
319	    relevance: >
320	      Directly addresses GRPO reward hacking in multi-objective settings.
321	      STA's ISR can be viewed as adding a structural objective to the
322	      correctness objective, making MO-GRPO's insights directly applicable.
323	    key_finding: >
324	      Standard GRPO normalizes after summing rewards, allowing high-variance
325	      objectives to dominate. MO-GRPO equalizes scales before aggregation.
326	
327	  - id: reward-hacking-survey
328	    title: "Reward Hacking in the Era of Large Models: Mechanisms, Emergent Misalignment, Challenges"
329	    authors: "Various"
330	    year: 2026
331	    venue: "arXiv 2604.13602"
332	    category: reward-hacking
333	    role: background
334	    relevance: >
335	      Comprehensive survey of reward hacking mechanisms in the LLM era.
336	      Provides theoretical framework for understanding why STA's structural
337	      reward is more robust than pure outcome-based reward.
338	    key_finding: >
339	      Reward hacking manifests through specification gaming, reward model
340	      exploitation, and emergent misalignment; structural verification
341	      rewards are more robust than learned reward models.
342	
343	  - id: energy-loss-reward-hacking
344	    title: "The Energy Loss Phenomenon in RLHF: A New Perspective on Mitigating Reward Hacking"
345	    authors: "Various"
346	    year: 2025
347	    venue: "ICML 2025"
348	    category: reward-hacking
349	    role: background
350	    relevance: >
351	      Identifies energy loss in LLM final layer as an indicator of reward
352	      hacking during RL. Provides complementary diagnostic to STA's
353	      structural reward approach.
354	    key_finding: >
355	      Energy loss in the final layer increases during RL and excessive
356	      increase characterizes reward hacking; EPPO algorithm penalizes
357	      this to mitigate hacking.
358

360	  # Category 6: FOL/Prolog formalization with LLMs
361	  # ============================================================
362	
363	  - id: folio
364	    title: "FOLIO: Natural Language Reasoning with First-Order Logic"
365	    authors: "Simeng Han et al."
366	    year: 2022
367	    venue: "arXiv 2209.00840 / EMNLP 2024"

379	    title: "ProofWriter: Generating Implications, Proofs, and Abductive Statements over Natural Language"

401	    relevance: >

# Literature Map for Solver Trace Ablation (STA)
# Categories:
#   1. neurosymbolic-rl: Neurosymbolic reasoning + RL/GRPO
#   2. reward-shaping: Reward shaping for code/formal verification
#   3. mutation-testing: Mutation testing in software engineering
#   4. intensional-analysis: Intensional program analysis
#   5. reward-hacking: Reward hacking / overoptimization
#   6. fol-formalization: FOL/Prolog formalization with LLMs

papers:

  # ============================================================
  # Category 1: Neurosymbolic reasoning + RL/GRPO
  # ============================================================

  - id: deepseek-r1
    title: "DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning"
    authors: "DeepSeek-AI"
    year: 2025
    venue: "arXiv 2501.12948 / Nature 2025"
    category: neurosymbolic-rl
    role: method-component

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": """"Phase 1 GRPO training: execution-only vs execution+STA reward.

Usage:
  # execution-only (GPU 0)
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python scripts/train_grpo.py \
    --model_path /root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-4B \
    --data_path data/proofwriter_fol_500.jsonl \
    --reward_mode execution_only --output_dir outputs/grpo_exec_only \
    --num_steps 100 --wandb_project solver-trace-ablation

  # execution+STA (GPU 1)
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python scripts/train_grpo.py \
    --model_path /root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-4B \
    --data_path data/proofwriter_fol_500.jsonl \
    --reward_mode execution_sta --output_dir outputs/grpo_exec_sta \
    --num_steps 100 --wandb_project solver-trace-ablation
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import random as _random
import re
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from datasets import Dataset
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TrainerCallback
from trl import GRPOConfig, GRPOTrainer

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from src.solvers.factory import get_solver
from src.sta.reward import _parse_formalization, fast_sta_reward, sta_reward
from src.sta.prolog_reward import (
    fast_prolog_sta_reward, parse_prolog_formalization, prolog_sta_reward,
)

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are a first-order logic (FOL) expert. "
    "Given natural language premises and a conclusion, formalize them into FOL.\n\n"
    "Output format:\n"
    "Premises:\n"
    "1. <FOL formula>\n"
    "2. <FOL formula>\n"
    "...\n"
    "Conclusion: <FOL formula>\n\n"
    "Use standard FOL notation with predicate-argument syntax: "
    "all x (P(x) -> Q(x)), exists x P(x), P(a) & Q(a), -P(a), P(a) | Q(a), P(a) -> Q(a)."
)

USER_TEMPLATE = (
    "Formalize the following in first-order logic.\n\n"
    "Context:\n{context}\n\n"
    "Statement to formalize:\n{question}"
)


PROLOG_SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are a Prolog logic programming expert. "
    "Given natural language premises and a conclusion, formalize them into Prolog.\n\n"
    "Output format:\n"
    "Facts/Rules:\n"
    "<fact_or_rule>.\n"
    "...\n\n"
    "Query: <goal>\n\n"
    "Use standard Prolog syntax: facts (predicate(args).), rules (head :- body.), "
    "variables start with uppercase, atoms/predicates start with lowercase."
)

PROLOG_USER_TEMPLATE = (
    "Formalize the following in Prolog.\n\n"
    "Context:\n{context}\n\n"
    "Statement to formalize:\n{question}"
)



def load_jsonl(path: str) -> list[dict]:
    data = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line:
                data.append(json.loads(line))
    return data


def build_dataset(data: list[dict]) -> Dataset:
    records = []
    for item in data:
        prompt = [
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": USER_TEMPLATE.format(
                context=item["context"], question=item["question"]
            )},
        ]
        records.append({
            "prompt": prompt,
            "id": item.get("id", ""),
            "answer": item.get("answer", ""),
            "fol_premises": json.dumps(item.get("fol_premises", [])),
            "fol_conclusion": item.get("fol_conclusion", ""),
        })
    return Dataset.from_list(records)

def build_prolog_dataset(data: list[dict]) -> Dataset:
    records = []
    for item in data:
        prompt = [
            {"role": "system", "content": PROLOG_SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": PROLOG_USER_TEMPLATE.format(
                context=item["context"], question=item["question"]
            )},
        ]
        records.append({
            "prompt": prompt,
            "id": item.get("id", ""),
            "answer": item.get("answer", ""),
            "prolog_premises": json.dumps(item.get("prolog_premises", [])),
            "prolog_query": item.get("prolog_query", ""),
        })
    return Dataset.from_list(records)



def strip_thinking(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"<think>.*?</think>\s*", "", text, flags=re.DOTALL).strip()


def extract_completion_text(completion) -> str:
    """Extract text from a completion (handles both string and conversational formats)."""
    if isinstance(completion, list):
        return completion[-1]["content"] if completion else ""
    return completion

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": """"Phase 1 GRPO training: execution-only vs execution+STA reward.

Usage:
  # execution-only (GPU 0)
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python scripts/train_grpo.py \
    --model_path /root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-4B \
    --data_path data/proofwriter_fol_500.jsonl \
    --reward_mode execution_only --output_dir outputs/grpo_exec_only \
    --num_steps 100 --wandb_project solver-trace-ablation

  # execution+STA (GPU 1)
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python scripts/train_grpo.py \
    --model_path /root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-4B \
    --data_path data/proofwriter_fol_500.jsonl \
    --reward_mode execution_sta --output_dir outputs/grpo_exec_sta \
    --num_steps 100 --wandb_project solver-trace-ablation
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import logging
import os
import random as _random
import re
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from datasets import Dataset
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TrainerCallback
from trl import GRPOConfig, GRPOTrainer

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from src.solvers.factory import get_solver
from src.sta.reward import _parse_formalization, fast_sta_reward, sta_reward
from src.sta.prolog_reward import (
    fast_prolog_sta_reward, parse_prolog_formalization, prolog_sta_reward,
)

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are a first-order logic (FOL) expert. "
    "Given natural language premises and a conclusion, formalize them into FOL.\n\n"
    "Output format:\n"
    "Premises:\n"
    "1. <FOL formula>\n"
    "2. <FOL formula>\n"
    "...\n"
    "Conclusion: <FOL formula>\n\n"
    "Use standard FOL notation with predicate-argument syntax: "
    "all x (P(x) -> Q(x)), exists x P(x), P(a) & Q(a), -P(a), P(a) | Q(a), P(a) -> Q(a)."
)

USER_TEMPLATE = (
    "Formalize the following in first-order logic.\n\n"
    "Context:\n{context}\n\n"
    "Statement to formalize:\n{question}"
)


PROLOG_SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are a Prolog logic programming expert. "
    "Given natural language premises and a conclusion, formalize them into Prolog.\n\n"
    "Output format:\n"
    "Facts/Rules:\n"
    "<fact_or_rule>.\n"
    "...\n\n"
    "Query: <goal>\n\n"
    "Use standard Prolog syntax: facts (predicate(args).), rules (head :- body.), "
    "variables start with uppercase, atoms/predicates start with lowercase."
)

PROLOG_USER_TEMPLATE = (
    "Formalize the following in Prolog.\n\n"
    "Context:\n{context}\n\n"
    "Statement to formalize:\n{question}"
)



def load_jsonl(path: str) -> list[dict]:
    data = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line:
                data.append(json.loads(line))
    return data


def build_dataset(data: list[dict]) -> Dataset:
    records = []
    for item in data:
        prompt = [
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": USER_TEMPLATE.format(
                context=item["context"], question=item["question"]
            )},
        ]
        records.append({
            "prompt": prompt,
            "id": item.get("id", ""),
            "answer": item.get("answer", ""),
            "fol_premises": json.dumps(item.get("fol_premises", [])),
            "fol_conclusion": item.get("fol_conclusion", ""),
        })
    return Dataset.from_list(records)

def build_prolog_dataset(data: list[dict]) -> Dataset:
    records = []
    for item in data:
        prompt = [
            {"role": "system", "content": PROLOG_SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": PROLOG_USER_TEMPLATE.format(
                context=item["context"], question=item["question"]
            )},
        ]
        records.append({
            "prompt": prompt,
            "id": item.get("id", ""),
            "answer": item.get("answer", ""),
            "prolog_premises": json.dumps(item.get("prolog_premises", [])),
            "prolog_query": item.get("prolog_query", ""),
        })
    return Dataset.from_list(records)



def strip_thinking(text: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"<think>.*?</think>\s*", "", text, flags=re.DOTALL).strip()


def extract_completion_text(completion) -> str:
    """Extract text from a completion (handles both string and conversational formats)."""
    if isinstance(completion, list):
        return completion[-1]["content"] if completion else ""
    return completion

1. ✅ **SWI-Prolog binary** installed
2. ✅ **PrologSolver** class
3. ✅ **Prolog STA reward** functions (full + fast)
4. ✅ **Prolog prompt template** — PROLOG_SYSTEM_PROMPT and PROLOG_USER_TEMPLATE instruct the model to output Prolog syntax
5. ✅ **build_prolog_dataset** — creates proper chat prompts for Prolog


6. ✅ **Training configs** — two configs ready
7. ✅ **Solver factory** supports "prolog"
8. ✅ **train_grpo.py** dispatches correctly for logic_type=prolog

The architecture is elegant: the model receives the same natural language problems but is prompted to generate Prolog instead of FOL, and the reward signal comes directly from whether SWI-Prolog can execute and prove the formalization—no ground truth Prolog clauses needed. This is the same execution-based RL approach as Prover9, just adapted for a different solver, which is the right design.

But there are some gaps to address. The main issue is that eval_sta.py is hardcoded for Prover9, so there's no way to run proper held-out evaluation on Prolog models after training. The step count defaults to 100 but can be overridden via CLI. The exec_sta config uses a 50/50 weight combination that didn't work well for Prover9, though Prolog might respond differently.     data = []

    return data

    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path, trust_remote_code=True)

content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"path\": \"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_3/projects/solver-trace-ablation/paper_framing.md\", \"content\": \"# Paper Framing — solver-trace-ablation\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (NLP and Symbolic Reasoning track)\\n- Fallback: EMNLP 2026 Findings\\n- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026\\n\\n## Core Claims (3 条 — 诊断/分析论文)\\n\\n### Claim 1: ISR as Reward Hacking Diagnostic\\nSolver Trace Ablation (STA) derives ISR (Intensional Structural Reward) via component necessity testing (leave-one-out ablation on solver inputs). ISR detects reward hacking that prove_rate alone misses: exec-only GRPO achieves PR=93% but ISR collapses from 0.6423 (100 steps) to 0.1324 (500 steps), quantifying structural degeneration invisible to the execution reward.\\n\\n**证据**:\\n- plan003: 100-step checkpoint held-out eval PR=32%, ISR=0.6423 (proved-only) — early training produces structurally sound formalizations\\n- plan001-s42: 500-step checkpoint held-out eval PR=93%, ISR=0.1324, median_ISR=0.0 — late training achieves high prove_rate via structural shortcuts\\n- 3-seed consistency: s42 conclusion embedding (ISR=0.123), s43 repetition collapse (PR=13%, ISR=0), s44 tautological collapse (PR=98%, ISR=0.57 fake-high, n_comp=2.04)\\n- Hacking taxonomy: 5 distinct modes identified and quantified (plan012 `hacking_characterization_report.md` + plan017 D027)\\n\\n### Claim 2: GRPO Saturation Mechanism\\nExec-only GRPO exhibits a saturation failure mode: when prove_rate → 1.0, reward_std → 0 and loss → 0, training effectively stalls. Any reward component introducing variance (ISR, random noise) prevents saturation but does not prevent hacking — it redirects hacking into different structural failure modes.\\n\\n**证据**:\\n- plan001 exec-only: PR saturation → loss=0 → learning stops (D014)\\n- plan013 random reward: PR=1.0 (prevents saturation) but 100% P→P tautological collapse (D018)\\n- plan002 additive ISR β=0.3: PR=18%, ISR=0.1427 — ISR bonus prevents saturation but causes repetitive cycling, lowest PR of all conditions (D020)\\n- plan005 convex combination: penalty effect confirmed — any ISR<1 reduces reward (D010)\\n- plan017 additive random β=0.3: eval PR=48%, ISR=0.045, comp=9.56 — \\\"complexity-without-utility\\\" mode (高 component 但 conclusion 不依赖 premises, 33% proved ISR=0). ISR 比 random 更差 (PR 18% vs 48%), ISR 信号对训练 actively misleading (D026/D027)\\n- ⚠️ **措辞约束 (Reviewer D027)**: plan013 (0.9·r_exec+0.1·random) vs plan017 (r_exec·(1+0.3·random)) 公式结构不同，不可简化为\\\"additive vs convex\\\"对照。plan017 vs plan002 的 ISR vs random 对比是纯净的（唯一变量是 random vs ISR）\\n\\n### Claim 3: Cross-Logic Generality (conditional on plan006)\\nSTA protocol is solver-agnostic: the 5-step derivation (pilot → collect shortcuts → classify → map RIP → design check) transfers to structurally different formal languages. Hacking modes and ISR diagnostic value replicate across FOL→Prover9 and Prolog→SWI-Prolog.\\n\\n**证据**: 待验证。plan006 Prolog GRPO 实验未启动。如果 plan006 无法复现 hacking + ISR 诊断，此 claim 降级为 future work。\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n- **Problem**: GRPO with execution-only rewards trains neurosymbolic formalizers that achieve high solve rates but produce structurally degenerate outputs (reward hacking). Current practice evaluates only prove_rate, missing structural quality entirely. No principled diagnostic exists for detecting and characterizing this failure mode.\\n- **Existing approaches & gaps**: Mellgren et al. (2025) hand-craft Prolog-specific structure penalties. EVOM (2026) uses scalar execution rewards only. ExecVerify/EGCA derive trace-level rewards for code, not formal logic. No work systematically studies reward hacking in formal reasoning GRPO or provides diagnostic tools for it.\\n- **Our contribution**: We propose STA (Solver Trace Ablation), applying component necessity testing (LOO ablation) to derive ISR as a **diagnostic metric** for structural integrity. Key findings:\\n  1. ISR quantifies hacking invisible to prove_rate (64% → 13% collapse over training)\\n  2. GRPO saturation creates a \\\"training trap\\\": PR→1 means no gradient signal, but adding any variance (ISR or random) redirects rather than prevents hacking\\n  3. Different reward formulations produce distinct, classifiable hacking strategies (5 modes identified)\\n  4. ISR measures syntactic component necessity, not semantic faithfulness — this boundary is important for practitioners\\n- **Actionable insights for practitioners**:\\n  1. Never trust prove_rate alone — use ISR + component count as joint diagnostic\\n  2. Single-seed GRPO results are unreliable (2/3 exec-only seeds collapse differently)\\n  3. Adding structural reward components can hurt prove_rate (penalty effect) or redirect hacking (saturation effect) — neither naïvely improves quality\\n  4. ISR is a structural diagnostic, not a semantic quality proxy\\n- **Headline result**: \\\"We demonstrate that GRPO-trained FOL formalizers achieving 93-98% prove rate produce structurally degenerate outputs detectable by ISR — a component necessity metric derived from solver trace ablation. Across 5 reward conditions and 3 seeds, we identify 5 distinct hacking strategies and a GRPO saturation mechanism that confounds all reward-augmentation approaches. ISR as training signal is worse than matched random noise (PR 18% vs 48%), confirming its value is strictly diagnostic.\\\"\\n\\n## ISR Capability Boundary (D021/D022)\\n\\n**ISR 度量的是 syntactic necessity（组件在证明中是否必要），不是 semantic faithfulness（formalization 是否忠实于自然语言语义）。**\\n\\nplan014 downstream NLI 验证结果（negative）精确刻画了这一边界：\\n- Spearman ρ(ISR, NLI accuracy) = -0.049 (p=0.187, 不显著)\\n- Best-of-N ISR selection vs random: +0.9pp (不显著)\\n- 主因：模型严重 true-bias (false accuracy=0%)，NLI accuracy 天花板仅 34.1%\\n\\n**论文处理**：ISR-as-downstream-quality-proxy 降级为 **Limitation / Future Work**。plan014 结果作为 negative result 保留，精确刻画 ISR 能力边界。\\n\\n## ISR-as-Reward Failure Log (D010→D020)\\n\\n以下路线已全面失败，论文不再 claim ISR 可改善训练：\\n- **凸组合** r = α·r_exec + β·r_exec·ISR, α+β=1：ISR<1 时永远是 penalty (plan005, D010)\\n- **Additive bonus β=0.3** r = r_exec·(1+0.3·ISR)：PR=18%, 最差条件 (plan002, D020)\\n- **Additive bonus β=0.1** r = r_exec·(1+0.1·ISR)：实验中 (plan002-b01)\\n- **Random reward** r = α·r_exec + β·r_exec·random：PR=100% 但 100% tautological (plan013, D018)\\n- **Additive random β=0.3** r = r_exec·(1+0.3·random)：PR=48%, 未坍缩但 complexity-without-utility (plan017, D026)\\n\\n这些 negative results 本身是论文贡献——展示了 structural reward integration 的失败模式。关键发现：ISR 比 matched random 更差 (PR 18% vs 48%)，说明 ISR 信号对训练 actively misleading 而非仅仅 noisy。\\n\\n## Venue Fit Risks\\n\\n- **EMNLP fit**: Diagnostic/analysis paper in NLP + formal reasoning track. Empirical findings + negative results are valued at EMNLP.\\n- **\\\"Just negative results\\\" risk**: Mitigate by providing actionable diagnostic framework (ISR + taxonomy) and mechanistic insight (GRPO saturation).\\n- **Single-logic risk**: If plan006 Prolog doesn't happen, paper is FOL-only. Mitigate by emphasizing depth of analysis (3 seeds × 4 conditions × 4 hacking modes).\\n- **\\\"Old wine\\\" risk**: ISR = LOO ablation. Claim novelty at application level (first systematic hacking diagnostic for formal reasoning GRPO) + empirical findings, not algorithm level.\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n1. **\\\"ISR is just LOO ablation — not novel\\\"** — Yes, explicitly acknowledge. Contribution is (a) applying it as hacking diagnostic for formal reasoning GRPO, (b) empirical taxonomy of hacking modes, (c) GRPO saturation mechanism analysis.\\n2. **\\\"No positive result — ISR doesn't improve training\\\"** — Correct; we frame ISR as diagnostic, not reward. The systematic failure of all ISR-as-reward attempts is itself informative (Section: ISR-as-Reward Failure Log).\\n3. **\\\"ISR is circular\\\"** — ISR is used for diagnosis/post-hoc analysis, not as optimization target. Component count analysis (mean=6.58 vs 2.04, p<0.0001) provides ISR-independent structural evidence.\\n4. **\\\"Only one logic type\\\"** — STA protocol is solver-agnostic; plan006 Prolog validates generality. If absent, acknowledge as limitation.\\n5. **\\\"500 steps too short\\\"** — plan016 extends to 1000+ steps. Pre-saturation learning curves show hacking onset occurs within 200-300 steps.\\n6. **\\\"3 seeds insufficient for statistical claims\\\"** — The 3-seed divergence (3 different hacking modes from same setup) is itself a finding, not a limitation. But statistical claims on mean ISR use 3-seed mean±std.\\n7. **\\\"Related work insufficient\\\"** — Expand to 25+ refs (literature_map.yaml has 29): reward hacking (Gao 2023, Skalse 2022), GRPO (Shao 2024), formal reasoning (LeanDojo, Baldur, AlphaProof), feature attribution (SHAP), FOLIO (Han 2022).\\n8. **\\\"RIP framework overstated\\\"** — Frame as \\\"component necessity testing inspired by mutation testing's RIP framework,\\\" only Propagation condition operationalized.\\n9. **\\\"Practitioners can't act on this\\\"** — 4 actionable insights listed in Story Spine. ISR + component count as joint diagnostic is immediately deployable.\\n10. **\\\"GRPO saturation is known\\\"** — General RL reward saturation is known (Gao et al. 2023). Our contribution is documenting the specific manifestation in GRPO for formal reasoning + showing that naïve fixes (adding variance) redirect rather than prevent hacking.\\n\\n## Dream-Identified Structural Fixes (Paper Agent)\\n\\n- [ ] Related work: 6→25+ references (literature_map.yaml now has 29)\\n- [ ] RIP framing: reframe as \\\"component necessity testing inspired by RIP\\\"\\n- [ ] \\\"Dense+automatic\\\" → \\\"conditionally dense\\\"\\n- [ ] Remove all \\\"Pareto-improving\\\" language\\n- [ ] Acknowledge ISR = LOO ablation, cite feature attribution literature\\n- [ ] Address ISR sparsity for unproved outputs explicitly\\n- [x] Convex combination → additive bonus (D010, then D020 confirmed all ISR-as-reward failed)\\n- [x] ISR downstream validation → Limitation/Future Work (D021/D022, plan014 negative)\\n- [x] Hacking taxonomy completed (plan012, 4 modes identified)\\n\", \"total_chars\": 9629, \"truncated\": false}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {}}"}

## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (NLP and Symbolic Reasoning track)
- Fallback: EMNLP 2026 Findings
- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026

## Core Claims (3 条 — 诊断/分析论文)

### Claim 1: ISR as Reward Hacking Diagnostic
Solver Trace Ablation (STA) derives ISR (Intensional Structural Reward) via component necessity testing (leave-one-out ablation on solver inputs). ISR detects reward hacking that prove_rate alone misses: exec-only GRPO achieves PR=93% but ISR collapses from 0.6423 (100 steps) to 0.1324 (500 steps), quantifying structural degeneration invisible to the execution reward.

**证据**:
- plan003: 100-step checkpoint held-out eval PR=32%, ISR=0.6423 (proved-only) — early training produces structurally sound formalizations
- plan001-s42: 500-step checkpoint held-out eval PR=93%, ISR=0.1324, median_ISR=0.0 — late training achieves high prove_rate via structural shortcuts
- 3-seed consistency: s42 conclusion embedding (ISR=0.123), s43 repetition collapse (PR=13%, ISR=0), s44 tautological collapse (PR=98%, ISR=0.57 fake-high, n_comp=2.04)
- Hacking taxonomy: 5 distinct modes identified and quantified (plan012 `hacking_characterization_report.md` + plan017 D027)

### Claim 2: GRPO Saturation Mechanism
Exec-only GRPO exhibits a saturation failure mode: when prove_rate → 1.0, reward_std → 0 and loss → 0, training effectively stalls. Any reward component introducing variance (ISR, random noise) prevents saturation but does not prevent hacking — it redirects hacking into different structural failure modes.

**证据**:
- plan001 exec-only: PR saturation → loss=0 → learning stops (D014)
- plan013 random reward: PR=1.0 (prevents saturation) but 100% P→P tautological collapse (D018)
- plan002 additive ISR β=0.3: PR=18%, ISR=0.1427 — ISR bonus prevents saturation but causes repetitive cycling, lowest PR of all conditions (D020)
- plan005 convex combination: penalty effect confirmed — any ISR<1 reduces reward (D010)
- plan017 additive random β=0.3: eval PR=48%, ISR=0.045, comp=9.56 — "complexity-without-utility" mode (高 component 但 conclusion 不依赖 premises, 33% proved ISR=0). ISR 比 random 更差 (PR 18% vs 48%), ISR 信号对训练 actively misleading (D026/D027)
- ⚠️ **措辞约束 (Reviewer D027)**: plan013 (0.9·r_exec+0.1·random) vs plan017 (r_exec·(1+0.3·random)) 公式结构不同，不可简化为"additive vs convex"对照。plan017 vs plan002 的 ISR vs random 对比是纯净的（唯一变量是 random vs ISR）

### Claim 3: Cross-Logic Generality (conditional on plan006)
STA protocol is solver-agnostic: the 5-step derivation (pilot → collect shortcuts → classify → map RIP → design check) transfers to structurally different formal languages. Hacking modes and ISR diagnostic value replicate across FOL→Prover9 and Prolog→SWI-Prolog.

**证据**: 待验证。plan006 Prolog GRPO 实验未启动。如果 plan006 无法复现 hacking + ISR 诊断，此 claim 降级为 future work。

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: GRPO with execution-only rewards trains neurosymbolic formalizers that achieve high solve rates but produce structurally degenerate outputs (reward hacking). Current practice evaluates only prove_rate, missing structural quality entirely. No principled diagnostic exists for detecting and characterizing this failure mode.
- **Existing approaches & gaps**: Mellgren et al. (2025) hand-craft Prolog-specific structure penalties. EVOM (2026) uses scalar execution rewards only. ExecVerify/EGCA derive trace-level rewards for code, not formal logic. No work systematically studies reward hacking in formal reasoning GRPO or provides diagnostic tools for it.
- **Our contribution**: We propose STA (Solver Trace Ablation), applying component necessity testing (LOO ablation) to derive ISR as a **diagnostic metric** for structural integrity. Key findings:
  1. ISR quantifies hacking invisible to prove_rate (64% → 13% collapse over training)
  2. GRPO saturation creates a "training trap": PR→1 means no gradient signal, but adding any variance (ISR or random) redirects rather than prevents hacking
  3. Different reward formulations produce distinct, classifiable hacking strategies (5 modes identified)
  4. ISR measures syntactic component necessity, not semantic faithfulness — this boundary is important for practitioners
- **Actionable insights for practitioners**:
  1. Never trust prove_rate alone — use ISR + component count as joint diagnostic
  2. Single-seed GRPO results are unreliable (2/3 exec-only seeds collapse differently)
  3. Adding structural reward components can hurt prove_rate (penalty effect) or redirect hacking (saturation effect) — neither naïvely improves quality
  4. ISR is a structural diagnostic, not a semantic quality proxy
- **Headline result**: "We demonstrate that GRPO-trained FOL formalizers achieving 93-98% prove rate produce structurally degenerate outputs detectable by ISR — a component necessity metric derived from solver trace ablation. Across 5 reward conditions and 3 seeds, we identify 5 distinct hacking strategies and a GRPO saturation mechanism that confounds all reward-augmentation approaches. ISR as training signal is worse than matched random noise (PR 18% vs 48%), confirming its value is strictly diagnostic."

## ISR Capability Boundary (D021/D022)

**ISR 度量的是 syntactic necessity（组件在证明中是否必要），不是 semantic faithfulness（formalization 是否忠实于自然语言语义）。**

plan014 downstream NLI 验证结果（negative）精确刻画了这一边界：
- Spearman ρ(ISR, NLI accuracy) = -0.049 (p=0.187, 不显著)
- Best-of-N ISR selection vs random: +0.9pp (不显著)
- 主因：模型严重 true-bias (false accuracy=0%)，NLI accuracy 天花板仅 34.1%

**论文处理**：ISR-as-downstream-quality-proxy 降级为 **Limitation / Future Work**。plan014 结果作为 negative result 保留，精确刻画 ISR 能力边界。

## ISR-as-Reward Failure Log (D010→D020)

以下路线已全面失败，论文不再 claim ISR 可改善训练：
- **凸组合** r = α·r_exec + β·r_exec·ISR, α+β=1：ISR<1 时永远是 penalty (plan005, D010)
- **Additive bonus β=0.3** r = r_exec·(1+0.3·ISR)：PR=18%, 最差条件 (plan002, D020)
- **Additive bonus β=0.1** r = r_exec·(1+0.1·ISR)：实验中 (plan002-b01)
- **Random reward** r = α·r_exec + β·r_exec·random：PR=100% 但 100% tautological (plan013, D018)
- **Additive random β=0.3** r = r_exec·(1+0.3·random)：PR=48%, 未坍缩但 complexity-without-utility (plan017, D026)

这些 negative results 本身是论文贡献——展示了 structural reward integration 的失败模式。关键发现：ISR 比 matched random 更差 (PR 18% vs 48%)，说明 ISR 信号对训练 actively misleading 而非仅仅 noisy。

## Venue Fit Risks

- **EMNLP fit**: Diagnostic/analysis paper in NLP + formal reasoning track. Empirical findings + negative results are valued at EMNLP.
- **"Just negative results" risk**: Mitigate by providing actionable diagnostic framework (ISR + taxonomy) and mechanistic insight (GRPO saturation).
- **Single-logic risk**: If plan006 Prolog doesn't happen, paper is FOL-only. Mitigate by emphasizing depth of analysis (3 seeds × 4 conditions × 4 hacking modes).
- **"Old wine" risk**: ISR = LOO ablation. Claim novelty at application level (first systematic hacking diagnostic for formal reasoning GRPO) + empirical findings, not algorithm level.

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

1. **"ISR is just LOO ablation — not novel"** — Yes, explicitly acknowledge. Contribution is (a) applying it as hacking diagnostic for formal reasoning GRPO, (b) empirical taxonomy of hacking modes, (c) GRPO saturation mechanism analysis.
2. **"No positive result — ISR doesn't improve training"** — Correct; we frame ISR as diagnostic, not reward. The systematic failure of all ISR-as-reward attempts is itself informative (Section: ISR-as-Reward Failure Log).
3. **"ISR is circular"** — ISR is used for diagnosis/post-hoc analysis, not as optimization target. Component count analysis (mean=6.58 vs 2.04, p<0.0001) provides ISR-independent structural evidence.
4. **"Only one logic type"** — STA protocol is solver-agnostic; plan006 Prolog validates generality. If absent, acknowledge as limitation.
5. **"500 steps too short"** — plan016 extends to 1000+ steps. Pre-saturation learning curves show hacking onset occurs within 200-300 steps.
6. **"3 seeds insufficient for statistical claims"** — The 3-seed divergence (3 different hacking modes from same setup) is itself a finding, not a limitation. But statistical claims on mean ISR use 3-seed mean±std.
7. **"Related work insufficient"** — Expand to 25+ refs (literature_map.yaml has 29): reward hacking (Gao 2023, Skalse 2022), GRPO (Shao 2024), formal reasoning (LeanDojo, Baldur, AlphaProof), feature attribution (SHAP), FOLIO (Han 2022).
8. **"RIP framework overstated"** — Frame as "component necessity testing inspired by mutation testing's RIP framework," only Propagation condition operationalized.
9. **"Practitioners can't act on this"** — 4 actionable insights listed in Story Spine. ISR + component count as joint diagnostic is immediately deployable.
10. **"GRPO saturation is known"** — General RL reward saturation is known (Gao et al. 2023). Our contribution is documenting the specific manifestation in GRPO for formal reasoning + showing that naïve fixes (adding variance) redirect rather than prevent hacking.

## Dream-Identified Structural Fixes (Paper Agent)

- [ ] Related work: 6→25+ references (literature_map.yaml now has 29)
- [ ] RIP framing: reframe as "component necessity testing inspired by RIP"
- [ ] "Dense+automatic" → "conditionally dense"
- [ ] Remove all "Pareto-improving" language
- [ ] Acknowledge ISR = LOO ablation, cite feature attribution literature
- [ ] Address ISR sparsity for unproved outputs explicitly
- [x] Convex combination → additive bonus (D010, then D020 confirmed all ISR-as-reward failed)
- [x] ISR downstream validation → Limitation/Future Work (D021/D022, plan014 negative)
- [x] Hacking taxonomy completed (plan012, 4 modes identified)
